key_insight: Variational circuits can already look statistically random while still remaining trainable, so randomness diagnostics and barren-plateau behavior are not the same thing.
engineering_relevance: For quantum algorithm design, this suggests depth and expressivity can be increased to capture useful structure without automatically triggering gradient collapse in the finite-depth regime studied.
method: Tested structured variational circuits on the 1D cluster-Ising model and a generalized toric code Hamiltonian.
Tracked complexity with Porter-Thomas statistics, entanglement-spectrum level statistics, and inverse participation ratios.
Compared these randomness indicators against optimization behavior and gradient scaling across circuit depth.
evidence_signal: As depth increased, the sampled states moved toward random-state or random-matrix-like signatures, yet variational optimization still worked and showed no exponential gradient suppression in the studied regime.
watch_item: The results apply to finite-depth, structured circuits in the models studied, so they should not be assumed to rule out barren plateaus in larger, less local, or deeper ansätze.
paper_title: Separation of Statistical Complexity and Trainability in Variational Quantum Circuits
